speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me more about your gait and limb ataxia: when did these symptoms first start, and have they been getting worse over time? Also, what is the most significant medical condition you have in your history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance suggests significant cerebellar involvement. To clarify your history and guide further testing: have you experienced any episodes of slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or double vision alongside these ataxic symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history; the combination of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use raises a significant concern for immune-mediated complications like PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy). Have you noticed any new symptoms such as confusion, personality changes, or worsening vision in addition to your ataxia? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
